reason: Verified verbatim: ConfigManager.java:147-149 (and the identical shape at 165-167 and 188-190) calls plugin.saveResource() on a bare `!settingsFile.exists()` test, with no `.corrupt` sibling probe and no on-disk quarantine marker; initSettingsFile() then lets settingsGate.load() decide, and that call returns OK for the freshly written template so the SEVERE branch at 151-155 is skipped. YamlFiles.quarantine (YamlFiles.java:139-146) uses Files.move(file, <name>.corrupt, REPLACE_EXISTING), i.e. a rename, so the original path really is vacant on the next start, and the only cross-run state is YamlFileGate's in-memory `private volatile boolean readOnly` (YamlFileGate.java:35) — a new gate object is built in the ConfigManager constructor (130-132) on every boot, and load() clears the latch on Status.OK (56-58), so nothing survives the restart. The next loadFromFile() then succeeds and sets settingsLoadedFromDisk = true (1397), so factory defaults become the authoritative disk configuration, exactly as the finding states. Recreating defaults for a genuinely absent file is intended first-run behavior (javadoc 143-144; display.yml acceptance note at 183; DefaultWaveAlignmentTest:32 documents the same `!exists` idiom), but this repository's own precedent treats the post-quarantine case as a defect: ShopConfigLoader.load() refuses to saveResource when isQuarantined() (ShopConfigLoader.java:93, definition at 206 = `gate.isReadOnly() || corruptFile(file).exists()`) and ShopConfigQuarantineRebuildTest:105-121 tests precisely the new-process case, while ArenaManager.ensureFile:841-845 states the same doctrine; ConfigManager is the one loader missing that check. 'Silently' is accurate for the recreation itself (saveResource logs nothing and validation passes, so the restart emits no line about the revert), although the previous run did emit the YamlFiles:144-145 SEVERE naming `game-settings.yml.corrupt`, and the admin content survives in that sibling — so impact is a factory-default revert plus later GUI saves cementing defaults, recoverable manually but not irreversible.
